# Best CRM Software for Small Businesses (2026): 19 CRMs Scored and Ranked

Published: August 21, 2026 · Reading time: about 56 minutes

19 CRMs scored on 12 categories Prices checked November 2026 How we score

Two CRMs finished 0.3 points apart at the top of this year’s scoring, and the whole gap comes down to one question: how much does price matter to you?

Zoho CRM is #1 of 18 at 86.6/100. HubSpot CRM is #2 of 18 at 86.3/100. A two-point change in Ease of Use alone would move an overall score by 0.32, more than the gap, so treat the top of this list as a near tie rather than a clear winner. Zoho leads because its Standard plan, at $14 per user per month on annual billing, already includes automated follow-up sequences, lead scoring and sales forecasting. HubSpot puts those on Sales Hub Professional, at $90 per seat per month plus a required $1,500 onboarding fee. HubSpot answers with the joint-highest Ease of Use score in the guide, marketing tools on the same contact record, and a free plan with email marketing included.

Freshsales (85.4/100) and Pipedrive (84.4/100) follow closely, both narrower in scope and built around the sales pipeline rather than marketing. monday CRM and Close are separated by 0.7 points in fifth and sixth. Salesforce and SugarAI (formerly SugarCRM) sit at the bottom, not because they are weak products but because they are priced and built for companies with a CRM administrator, which most small businesses don’t have.

Every entry below stands on its own: what the product is built around, what its plans cost and on what billing basis, what users and reviewers report, and who should skip it. If you’d rather start from your own numbers, the CRM Recommendation Quiz narrows the field by team size and goals, and the CRM Cost Calculator prices a shortlist for your seat count.

Editorial note: This guide used to include Zendesk Sell. Zendesk announced on September 9, 2025 that it will retire Sell on August 31, 2027, and named Pipedrive as its migration partner (Zendesk’s support announcement). A product with a shutdown date isn’t a fair pick for a new buyer, so Nutshell took its slot. If you’re a current Sell customer, the Pipedrive entry below covers what the migration does and doesn’t carry over.

## Why Trust Our Recommendations?

We haven’t tested these 18 CRMs ourselves yet, and we’d rather say so up front. This guide is built from public sources: each vendor’s pricing pages, plan comparisons and help documentation, App Store and Google Play listings, user reviews on Trustpilot and vendor forums, small-business review themes on G2 and Capterra, and reviews from publications such as TechRadar, PCMag and TechRepublic. Each claim names its source where it’s used, with the date we checked it.

What we add is a single scoring system applied the same way to all 18. It’s built for small-business fit rather than raw capability: a team with no CRM administrator, a real budget and no time for a three-month rollout. That’s why Salesforce, which can do almost anything, ranks #17 of 18. Its documented gates (a 5-flow cap on Pro Suite, a paid API add-on, annual-only billing above Starter) land exactly where a small team would buy.

## How We Evaluated Each CRM

Every CRM gets a 0 to 100 score in twelve categories, and the weighted sum is its overall score. The weights favor what decides small-business success: a tool people use without an admin, at a price that doesn’t punish growth.

| Category | Weight | Why it’s weighted this way |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ease of Use | 16% | No in-house administrator to smooth over a difficult interface |
| Sales | 14% | The core job of a CRM, regardless of company size |
| Value for Money | 10% | A small business has far less room to absorb rising costs |
| Implementation | 10% | A multi-month rollout is a cost a lean team can’t easily absorb |
| Automation | 10% | Saves the most time for teams too small to hire more people |
| Marketing | 8% | Often has to stand in for a separate platform a small business can’t afford |
| Reporting | 6% | Useful, but most small businesses need dashboards, not a BI suite |
| Integrations | 6% | Matters less than at enterprise scale, since fewer systems need connecting |
| Support | 6% | Fills the gap left by not having in-house CRM expertise |
| Mobile | 6% | Owners and reps are often out of the office without a laptop |
| Customization | 4% | Deep configurability often goes unused, and sometimes becomes a liability at this scale |
| AI | 4% | A useful extra today, but still an immature, unproven category |

Each category score comes with written reasoning, and in this guide we lead with the evidence behind it: the plan limits, prices, app store ratings and user reports that a score should rest on. Where our research questioned a score, we kept the score and flagged it for review rather than adjust it here.

What decides the top spot. Zoho and HubSpot trade category wins almost evenly. Zoho’s lead in Value for Money (98 against 62) is worth 3.6 weighted points on its own, plus smaller edges in Reporting, Customization and Automation. HubSpot gets most of that back through Ease of Use (95 against 84), Marketing (97 against 84), Mobile, Sales, Implementation, Support and AI. Take Value for Money out of the model and HubSpot would lead by about 3 points. Leave it in, as we do for small businesses, and Zoho is ahead by 0.3.

## Detailed CRM Reviews

The entries run from the highest overall score to the lowest. The top six get the most space, because that’s where most small businesses will shortlist and where the differences are finest.

### Zoho CRM

Best for budget-conscious teams that want to build their own sales process into the CRM.

Free plan paid from $14/user/mo

86.6 out of 100

Zoho’s Standard edition costs $14 per user per month on annual billing, and Zoho’s pricing and feature-availability pages show what that buys: cadences (Zoho’s name for automated follow-up sequences), lead scoring rules, sales forecasting, and up to five pipelines. HubSpot puts sequences, scoring and forecasting on its $90 Professional plan, and Freshsales puts scoring and sequences on its $39 Pro plan.

Best for

Small teams with a defined sales process and someone willing to configure it.

Skip it if

you want a CRM that works on day one with no setup choices.

More: scores, pricing, strengths and limitations Show less

The limits sit at both ends of the range. The free edition stops at 3 users and 5,000 records, and Standard caps you at 100,000 records and 250 mass emails a day. Blueprint, which forces deals through defined stages in order, starts on Professional ($23), and a sandbox for testing changes needs Enterprise ($40). Zia, Zoho’s AI assistant, moved its core features (record summaries, writing help, prediction builders) down to Professional in March 2026, according to a Zoho community announcement; Zoho’s own comparison table still lists them from Enterprise, so check the edition before you count on them.

Outside views split on how hard it is to learn. TechRadar’s 2026 small-business guide names Zoho its easiest-to-use pick, while Startups.co.uk lists a steeper learning curve and a time-consuming setup. They agree on support: TechRadar’s review calls it inconsistent, Startups.co.uk notes limited phone support on lower plans, and Zoho sells Premium support separately. Small-business reviewers on G2 and Capterra (reviews from April 2025 to October 2026) repeat the same split: they credit Zoho with value and customization, and complain about busy menus, the learning curve and slow replies for anyone without premium support. On mobile, the iPhone app holds 4.4 stars from about 2,700 ratings on the US App Store (October 22, 2026), updated twice in October 2026.

What puts it first. Price against depth. Zoho scores 98/100 on Value for Money, the highest in our ranking, and that single category is worth more than HubSpot’s leads in ease and marketing combined. Overall it’s #1 of 18 at 86.6/100. If your team has no one willing to own setup, a lead that narrow isn’t worth much.

Pricing

Free edition for up to 3 users and 5,000 records. Standard $14 per user per month billed annually ($20 monthly), Professional $23 ($35 monthly), Enterprise $40 ($50 monthly), Ultimate $52 ($65 monthly). As checked on October 22, 2026. The free trial is 15 days, per Zoho’s sign-up page.

Strengths

- Sequences
- Scoring and forecasting on the $14 plan. Workflow rules on every edition
- Including 10 per module on Free. Customization that scales to 100 custom modules on Enterprise and 500 on Ultimate. Native links to Zoho Books, Desk, and Campaigns

Limitations

- Blueprint and the core AI features need Professional. TechRadar
- Startups.co.uk and recent G2 and Capterra reviewers all flag uneven support
- Faster support costs extra. More setup decisions up front than HubSpot or Pipedrive

Read Zoho CRM’s full review →

### HubSpot CRM

Best for small businesses that want sales and marketing on one contact record.

Free plan paid from $20/user/mo

86.3 out of 100

HubSpot’s free CRM gives two users 1,000 contacts, email marketing with 2,000 HubSpot-branded sends a month, a live-chat widget for your website and meeting links, with no time limit and no card required, per HubSpot’s pricing pages. The catch is automation: the free plan allows one automated email action. Every paid Hub (Sales, Marketing, Service) then adds tools on top of that same shared record, which is the reason to pick HubSpot over a sales-only tool.

Marketing-led small businesses and teams that will grow into one platform.

Skip it if

you need sequences or forecasting on a tight budget.

More: scores, pricing, strengths and limitations Show less

The price ladder is the documented limit, more than the feature list. Sales Hub Starter is $20 per seat per month on annual or monthly billing (HubSpot is currently offering new customers $7 a seat a month billed annually, or $10 monthly, for a limited time) and adds 15 pipelines and up to 50 workflows with restricted triggers, but no sequences, lead scoring, custom reports or forecasting. Those arrive on Professional at $90 per seat ($100 monthly) plus a mandatory $1,500 one-time onboarding fee, and custom objects need Enterprise. Quotes have left Sales Hub altogether: since September 2026, HubSpot’s knowledge base says new quotes need Revenue Hub Professional, an extra seat at $85 a month on annual billing ($95 monthly) per its pricing page. AI features and many workflow actions now draw on HubSpot Credits: 500 a month on Starter and 3,000 on Professional, with extra credits at $0.010 each and no rollover. Since October 15, 2026, admins can cap credit spend.

HubSpot’s own support for its customers follows the same ladder. HubSpot’s pricing page lists email support on Starter and phone support from Professional, and TechRadar’s review counts limited live support on entry plans and a confusing credit system among its cons. Two-factor login is compulsory on every paid account, per HubSpot’s security FAQ (October 2026).

User reports pull in two directions. The iPhone app holds 4.7 stars from about 16,000 ratings. On Trustpilot, HubSpot scores 1.5 from 1,181 reviews, and several reviews from August to October 2026 describe auto-renewals reviewers didn’t expect, renewals at the old tier after a downgrade request, and support waits of three to seven days. Trustpilot draws unhappy customers more than happy ones, but billing and renewal complaints also turn up in HubSpot’s own community forum and an App Store review, and G2 and Capterra reviewers from 2025 and 2026 describe modular pricing that climbs with every seat and tier while praising how fast new hires pick it up. Read the renewal terms before you sign.

What keeps it second. HubSpot scores 95/100 on Ease of Use, joint-highest in the guide, and 97 on Marketing, the highest. It loses the top spot on Value for Money, where its 62 is the lowest in our top six. Overall it’s #2 of 18 at 86.3/100. If the features you need sit on the free plan, HubSpot is the better buy than Zoho. On paid plans Zoho costs less at every step, from $14 for Standard against $20 for Starter, and far less once you need sequences or forecasting.

Pricing

Free plan for up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts. Sales Hub Starter $20 per seat per month, billed annually or monthly; Professional $90 per seat billed annually ($100 monthly) plus a required $1,500 onboarding fee; Enterprise from $150 per seat on an annual commitment, plus a required $3,500 onboarding fee. As checked on October 22, 2026.

Strengths

- The most useful free plan for marketing
- With email sends and a website chat widget included. Sales and marketing share one record. A marketplace of more than 2
- 000 apps. No seat minimum on Starter

Limitations

- Sequences, scoring
- Forecasting jump from $20 to $90 per seat plus onboarding. Quotes need a separate Revenue Hub seat. Credits meter AI
- Some automation. HubSpot’s own live support is thin below Professional. Recurring billing
- Renewal complaints in user reviews

### Freshsales

Best for small sales teams that want calling, chat and email inside the deal record.

from $9/user/mo billed annually

85.4 out of 100

Freshsales puts a phone line in the CRM. Its Growth plan, $9 per user per month on annual billing, includes built-in calling with call logs and recordings, website chat and email, with SMS and WhatsApp as further channels, per Freshworks’ pricing and features pages. That makes it one of the cheapest ways in this guide to give a whole team calling inside the contact record.

Best for

Sales teams of two to twenty who sell by phone and email.

Skip it if

marketing campaigns need to live in the CRM.

More: scores, pricing, strengths and limitations Show less

The plan tiers decide how far it goes. Growth has one Kanban pipeline view and what Freshworks calls “basic workflows”. Contact scoring, deal insights, sales sequences, territory management and multiple pipelines need Pro at $39. Custom modules, a sandbox, audit logs and forecasting insights need Enterprise at $59. Quotes (branded documents) cost $19 per user per month on top, and the Freddy AI Agent for website chat is billed at $49 per 100 sessions. Some reviews still mention a paid Freddy AI Copilot add-on; Freshworks’ pricing page no longer lists it, so don’t budget for it.

We found no Freshsales free plan on its pricing page. Third-party reports say the three-user free plan closed to new sign-ups in July 2026, though at least one Freshworks page from June 2026 still describes it. The pricing page itself offers a 21-day trial with no card.

Publications rate it highly. Startups.co.uk ranked it first among small-business CRMs in November 2025 and wrote that “Freshsales has one of the best small business offerings”. We agree on value: $9 and $39 plans with no seat minimum are hard to beat for a sales-only team. The weak spot both TechRadar pieces flag is integrations, which TechRadar’s review counts at about 30 native ones; Freshworks itself says “over 100 apps”. One business note matters for a long-term buyer: Freshworks said in May 2026 it will run its customer-experience business, which includes Freshsales, for profitability rather than growth, as investment shifts to its IT products (Diginomica).

What separates it. Freshsales trails HubSpot by 0.9 points and leads Pipedrive by 1.0. Against HubSpot it wins on Value for Money (92 against 62) and gives more than that back on Marketing (78 against 97), Automation, Integrations and AI. Overall it’s #3 of 18 at 85.4/100. The iPhone app holds 4.5 stars from 523 ratings, and Freshworks says the mobile app works offline. Freshworks’ help center also lists single sign-on on every plan, rare at this price, though that article dates from 2023, and its QuickBooks and Xero links only display invoices inside the CRM rather than syncing them.

Pricing

No free plan. Growth $9 per user per month billed annually ($11 monthly), Pro $39 ($47 monthly), Enterprise $59 ($71 monthly). Annual prices as checked on October 22, 2026; monthly prices from the pricing page’s monthly toggle, checked October 23, 2026.

Strengths

- Calling
- Website chat and email from the $9 plan. Scoring and sequences at $39
- Well below HubSpot’s equivalent tier. No seat minimum. Quick to adopt
- Per Startups.co.uk, and TechRadar

Limitations

- Email marketing lives in a separate product (Freshmarketer). Fewer native integrations than HubSpot or Zoho. Quotes and the chat AI agent cost extra. A small
- Merged Freshworks profile on Trustpilot (1.3 from 120 reviews) carries complaints about slow support, and billing

### Pipedrive

Best for sales-led teams that run everything from a visual pipeline.

from $14/user/mo billed annually

84.4 out of 100

Every Pipedrive plan, including the $14 Lite plan, gets customizable pipelines, Insights reports, the mobile apps and single sign-on. What changes as you pay more is how much the pipeline does by itself, and Pipedrive’s usage-limits page spells it out. Lite has no automations or sequences, 30 custom fields and 15 reports per user. Growth ($39 per seat annual, $49 monthly) adds 50 automations, 5 sequences and a forecast view. Premium ($59) adds AI email writing, multiple dashboards, permission sets and phone support.

Small sales teams whose day runs on deal stages.

Skip it if

you want marketing, sales and service in one tool.

More: scores, pricing, strengths and limitations Show less

That makes Growth the realistic entry point for most teams. Two-way email sync starts there too: on Lite, email reaches the CRM only through Smart Bcc, per Pipedrive’s help center (September 2026). Pipedrive’s own pricing page nudges the same way: its pricing FAQ says implementation is free on plans costing over $400 a year, which a Growth seat clears and a Lite seat doesn’t. Marketing is the clear gap. Email campaigns are a paid Campaigns add-on from $13.33 a month, and in August 2026 Pipedrive announced it is acquiring Outfunnel, the top-rated marketing-sync app on its marketplace, so the marketing side may change. On the AI side, Nova, a meeting tool that records calls and drafts summaries and suggested CRM updates, has been included in every plan at no extra cost since September 16, 2026, per Pipedrive’s announcement.

TechRadar’s April 2026 update calls Pipedrive “the most natural feeling CRM for sales-first teams”. We agree on the pipeline, which the plan limits and user reviews back up, but not with every detail in that review: its 10-user minimum on Ultimate doesn’t appear on Pipedrive’s pricing page. On Trustpilot, Pipedrive scores 4.4 from 3,463 reviews, with 2026 reviewers praising onboarding help and ease of use and single complaints about a messy migration and billing after cancellation. Capterra reviewers writing in 2026 most often complain about the Campaigns add-on, citing sending limits and account verification blocks. Mobile has slipped: Google Play now shows 4.0 from about 3,600 reviews and the US App Store 3.8 from 677 ratings (October 23, 2026).

What separates it. Pipedrive scores 95/100 on Sales and matches HubSpot’s 95 on Ease of Use, but its Marketing score of 48 is the lowest in our top six. Overall it’s #4 of 18 at 84.4/100, 1.0 behind Freshsales, which includes calling and has a cheaper Pro tier.

A note for Zendesk Sell customers: Zendesk named Pipedrive its official migration partner, and its announcement says Pipedrive built tools for the switch and will help set up a comparable configuration. Two limits are worth knowing before you go. Sell’s export covers leads, contacts, deals, notes, tasks and smart lists, but not activity history, appointments, emails, call logs or documents, and exports stay available for 30 days. Your Sell data is deleted when the subscription ends or on August 31, 2027, whichever comes first. If your needs have changed since you chose Sell, compare Pipedrive with Nutshell and Freshsales before you move.

Pricing

No free plan; 14-day trial with no card. Lite $14 per seat per month billed annually ($24 monthly), Growth $39 ($49 monthly), Premium $59 ($79 monthly), Ultimate $79 ($99 monthly). Annual prices as checked on October 22, 2026; monthly prices from the pricing page’s monthly toggle, checked October 23, 2026.

Strengths

- Clear
- Stage-based pipeline on every plan. Generous Growth plan for automations. Free implementation help from Growth up. AI meeting notes (Nova) on every plan. Offline use in the mobile apps

Limitations

- Lite has no automation or two-way email sync. Marketing needs an add-on or a second tool. No custom objects at any tier. Mobile ratings sit at 4.0 or below on both stores

### monday CRM

Best for teams of three or more that run sales and project work on the same boards.

from $12/user/mo billed annually

81.4 out of 100

monday CRM sells seats in bundles, starting at three, and its plan limits are written in the language of its work platform: boards, columns, dashboards and monthly automation actions. Basic ($12 per seat per month annual) has unlimited pipelines but caps active contacts and deals at 1,000, gives one custom dashboard, five columns per board, and no automations or integration actions. Standard ($17 annual, $25 monthly) adds 250 automation and 250 integration actions a month, two-way Gmail and Outlook sync and 10,000 contacts. Pro ($28) raises automations to 25,000 a month and adds mass email and email sequences.

Agencies and operations-heavy teams of three or more.

you’re a solo seller or want a CRM that works without designing boards.

More: scores, pricing, strengths and limitations Show less

So the useful plan is Standard or Pro, and a four-person team can end up paying for a five-seat bundle, per monday’s own seat-pricing article. Email campaigns are a separate product, monday campaigns, from $50 a month. AI features (a calling agent, a lead-sourcing agent, an AI notetaker) are listed from Standard, but each plan’s AI credit allowance isn’t published, and monday moved to a seat-and-credit pricing model in May 2026.

The three-seat minimum is the one complaint we can call common: it shows up on Trustpilot, in App Store reviews and as a con in TechRadar’s review, which otherwise praises the visual interface and no-code automation builder. Small-business reviewers on Capterra (mostly 2025 and 2026) widen that into the most common complaint overall: the plan structure, from the seat minimum to features held for higher tiers. The 4.8-star iPhone rating from about 48,000 ratings, and 4.7 from about 45,000 reviews on Google Play, belong to monday.com’s general work-platform app, which also opens CRM boards, not to a CRM-specific app. Company context: monday cut about 20% of its workforce in July 2026, mostly in down-market sales roles, and said it will rely more on partners for smaller customers (MarketBeat’s earnings-call coverage).

Best CRM Software 2026: Full Comparison | SoftDecider

# Best CRM Software 2026: Full Comparison

 You exported a thousand contacts out of a spreadsheet last night, and this morning two people edited the file at once. That is usually the week teams start shopping for a CRM. HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and Zoho all solve the problem, but their 2026 price ladders, free tiers and contract terms diverge far more than their landing pages admit. 

 Last Updated: 2026-11-07 Overall Rating: 4.5/5 CRMs Compared: 4 

 Edited & Reviewed by Guillaume Acloque 

## Listen to This Article

Four CRMs cover most buying situations in 2026: HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and Zoho. This comparison uses each vendor's published pricing pages, verified in October 2026, rather than lab testing. HubSpot wins for most teams starting free: the CRM costs nothing, Starter lists at twenty dollars per seat per month, and marketing, sales and service share one database. Zoho is the value pick, with a real free plan for three users and paid tiers from fourteen dollars. Pipedrive rebuilt its lineup this year into four plans, Lite, Growth, Premium and Ultimate, running from fourteen to seventy-nine dollars per seat, and it still has the cleanest visual pipeline of the group. Salesforce scales furthest, from a twenty-five dollar Starter Suite up to full Sales Cloud editions at five hundred and fifty dollars per user, but it expects admin time in return. The article runs the five-seat and ten-seat cost math, flags mandatory onboarding fees, and names the catches in every free tier.

## Quick Answer

 Best for most teams: HubSpot CRM. A free tier that is a real CRM, Starter at $20 per seat monthly, and marketing, sales and service data in one database. Budget for the $1,500 onboarding fee if you ever move up to Sales Hub Professional. 

 Best value once you pay: Zoho CRM. $14 per user monthly on Standard annual billing, month-to-month terms available, and a free plan covering exactly 3 users underneath. 

 Best for sales-only teams: Pipedrive. Its rebuilt 2026 lineup runs $14 to $79 per seat, and the visual pipeline remains the easiest to operate without training. 

 Best at scale: Salesforce. Starter Suite at $25 per user monthly is a reasonable entry, with a clear path to full Sales Cloud editions when thousands of reps and deep customization arrive.

## How We Picked

 SoftDecider does not run a software test lab. Every price and plan limit in this comparison comes from vendor pricing pages verified in October 2026, cross-checked against the published product catalogs of HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and Zoho. Where third-party articles contradicted the vendor's own page, the vendor page won, which matters more than usual this year. 

 Four criteria drove the ranking. Real entry cost first, calculated per seat on annual billing and again for a 5-person team, since per-seat stickers hide team totals. The automation tier second, because that is where every vendor's pricing actually bites. Contract flexibility third, including onboarding fees and whether month-to-month terms exist. Free tier honesty last, meaning what the free plan caps rather than what the marketing page promises. 

## Detailed Reviews

### #1 HubSpot CRM

 HubSpot is the platform choice of the four. The free CRM covers contacts, deal pipelines, forms and email with usage caps, and the first paid step, Starter, bills at $20 per seat monthly or $7 on annual terms, with the annual rate reserved for new customers. A Starter subscription removes HubSpot branding and includes 500 platform credits plus 1,000 marketing contacts, which is enough for a small team to run real campaigns rather than a trial. 

 The advantage compounds when marketing matters. HubSpot sells separate hubs for sales, service, marketing and content, but they share one database, so a lead's email opens, support tickets and deal stage sit on the same record. Seat pricing follows the catalog: Core seats run $20 at Starter up to $75 at Enterprise, whereas full Sales seats cost $100 to $150 at Professional and Enterprise levels. 

 Where it falls short: the ladder turns steep at Professional. Sales Hub Professional costs $90 per seat monthly on an annual commitment, and HubSpot charges a mandatory one-time onboarding fee of $1,500 at that tier, $3,500 at Enterprise. Mixing subscription levels in one account reprices every core seat to the highest tier, a rule most buyers discover only on their first invoice. Marketing contacts are billed separately from seats, so list growth raises costs on its own. HubSpot's October 2026 flexible-pricing update loosens one corner of this: AI spend caps and seat-to-credit swaps give buyers a lever on the credit lines that were hardest to forecast. 

Best for: Teams that want to start free, keep marketing and sales in one system, and can watch the Professional-tier cliff before climbing it.

 New October 2026 

HubSpot adds AI spend caps and seat-to-credit swaps

HubSpot's October 2026 pricing update adds spend caps on AI credits, seat-to-credit swaps and flexible payment options. The change answers the cost criticism in this review directly: credit-based AI features were the hardest line of a HubSpot invoice to forecast. Source →

### #2 Zoho CRM

Best Value Paid CRM

 Zoho CRM is the budget workhorse. Annual billing runs $14 per user on Standard, $23 on Professional, $40 on Enterprise and $52 on Ultimate, and unlike every rival here except Salesforce's Starter, Zoho also sells month-to-month terms at $20, $35, $50 and $65 with no contract. Underneath sits a free plan for exactly 3 users that includes 5,000 API calls per day, 10 custom email templates and data export up to 10 times, so a tiny team can operate for years without paying. 

 The functional steps between tiers are legible, which is rarer than it sounds. Professional brings Blueprint, Zoho's guided sales-process automation, along with inventory management and 500 daily emails. Enterprise adds the Zia AI assistant, custom modules and 250 roles. Buyers running the wider Zoho suite can bundle everything into Zoho CRM Plus at $57 per user monthly, which undercuts buying those services separately. 

 Where it falls short: the interface carries two decades of features, and new users feel it. Pipedrive teaches itself in an afternoon; Zoho rewards configuration effort with capability but charges that effort up front. Zia AI sits behind the $40 Enterprise tier, so the advertised AI arrives only two steps into the ladder, and role limits scale with spend, from 5 roles on Standard to 250 on Enterprise. 

Best for: Cost-conscious teams of 3 to 30 that want tiered automation and month-to-month freedom instead of platform polish.

 New October 2026 

Zoho presents its agentic AI strategy in Seoul

At an October 26 media roundtable ahead of its Zoholics 2026 conference in Korea, Zoho laid out its plan to connect its 60-plus business applications through agentic AI. For CRM buyers, the relevant question is how much of that roadmap lands in Zoho CRM tiers they can actually afford. Source →

### #3 Pipedrive

Best Pipeline Simplicity

 Pipedrive is a pipeline-first CRM, built around a kanban board that salespeople actually maintain. Its 2026 lineup replaced the old five-tier ladder with four plans: Lite at $14, Growth at $39, Premium at $59 and Ultimate at $79 per seat monthly on annual billing, with annual terms saving up to 42 percent against monthly. If you have read that Pipedrive sells Essential, Advanced, Professional and Power plans, you have read an outdated article; the vendor retired those names this year. 

 The functional map moved with the rebrand. Lite handles leads, deals, contacts and calendar sync, but automation starts at Growth, which adds full two-way email sync, tracking, sequences and workflow automation. Premium bundles lead capture and routing, custom scoring, AI email tools and contracts with e-signatures. Add-ons remain for extras: Campaigns from $13.33 monthly, Projects from $16, Web Visitors from $41. Implementation is included free on any plan above $400 per year. 

 Where it falls short: Lite at $14 ships without automation, and unlocking sequences and workflows means Growth at $39, close to triple the entry rate. There is no free tier, only a 14-day trial, so evaluating beyond two weeks means paying. Marketing exists as add-ons rather than a native strength, and a team needing sequences plus campaigns plus web visitor identification can end up paying closer to HubSpot money than the $14 sticker suggests. 

Best for: Founder-led sales teams that want the deal board to be the whole product, without paying for marketing machinery they will not use.

 New October 2026 

Pipedrive patched its PHP services same-day

Pipedrive's security team patched its PHP-based services against the October 21 critical CVEs the same day, and the status update confirms no customer action was required. Source →

### #4 Salesforce

 Salesforce is the ceiling option. The company now lists a Free Suite at $0, with Starter Suite as the real entry at $25 per user monthly, billable month-to-month or annually, and Slack Free bundled in. Full Slack Business+ waits for Sales Cloud Core. Pro Suite, at $100 per user monthly, adds process automation, custom apps and AppExchange access, but it requires an annual contract. Full Sales Cloud editions run far higher: Core at $195, Advanced at $395 and Max at $550 per user monthly, and regional listings carry local-currency prices, with Max listed at 550 euros per user in the EU. 

 What that money buys is headroom no rival matches. Custom objects, flows and the AppExchange marketplace mean the CRM can be shaped into whatever the business becomes, and companies scale from a two-person startup on Starter to thousands of reps without replatforming. For regulated industries and complex sales organizations, that flexibility is the product. 

 Where it falls short: Starter Suite is deliberately shallow, capping out at basic automation and simple email campaigns, so growth pushes buyers toward Pro Suite's annual contract quickly. Getting value past the entry tiers usually requires an administrator, whether in-house or billed by a partner, and per-user costs at scale dwarf the rest of this comparison. A 20-person team on Pro Suite pays $24,000 a year before any customization work begins. 

Best for: Organizations that already know they will need deep customization, integration and governance, and can staff for it.

 New October 2026 

Salesforce agrees to acquire Braze

On October 20, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze, the customer engagement platform. The deal adds a cross-channel messaging specialist to the stack around the CRM; no closing date was announced, and nothing in the pricing table above changes today. Source →

 New October 2026 

Salesforce invests $1 billion in Spain

Salesforce announced a $1 billion investment in Spain on October 19, including a new Madrid headquarters, to expand its European AI operations. EU buyers comparing vendors here get a signal about local support and data capacity, not a pricing change. Source →

## Which CRM Fits Your Situation?

 The same four products win or lose depending on who is buying. These are the situations we get asked about most, matched to the 2026 price data above. 

### If you are a founder testing whether a CRM pays off at all

 Start with Zoho's free plan if you are exactly 3 people, or HubSpot's free tier if you want the marketing tools attached. Both stay free rather than converting to a timed demo. Move when you hit their walls, and not before: Zoho's wall is the 3-user count, HubSpot's is usage caps plus branding on every customer-facing email. 

### If you run a 5-person sales team that lives in email

 Pipedrive Growth at $39 per seat is built for you: two-way email sync, open tracking and automated follow-up sequences tied directly to deal stages. HubSpot Starter covers the same team for $100 a month at list price, but its sequences and full tracking arrive at Sales Professional, where the 5-seat bill becomes $450 monthly plus a $1,500 onboarding fee. 

### If marketing and sales must share one system

 HubSpot is the only answer of the four that does this natively, since its hubs share a single database and contact record. Accept the trade-off honestly: contact-based pricing means costs grow with your email list even when headcount stays flat. Zoho CRM Plus is the budget alternative at $57 per user, bundling campaigns and social alongside the CRM, at the cost of a steeper learning curve. 

### If you sell complex deals and expect to customize everything

 Salesforce from Starter Suite upward, with eyes open. The $25 entry exists so you can start small, but the real destination is Pro Suite or Core with an admin budget attached. Teams that skip the admin allocation usually end up paying Salesforce prices for a system nobody has time to configure, which is the most expensive outcome of all. 

## Does Any Free CRM Actually Stay Free?

 Marketing pages say free; plan documents say otherwise. Here is what each vendor's published limits reveal about the fine print. 

### HubSpot free: free forever, capped and branded

 The free CRM carries no time limit and no credit card requirement, but custom properties stop at 10, marketing contacts at 1,000, and HubSpot branding stays on every email, form and live chat. Community support only. It is a real product with a ceiling, not a trap, and the ceiling is low enough that an active team feels it within a quarter. 

### Zoho free: the most honest wall in the market

 Three users, forever, with 5,000 API calls per day and export rights up to 10 times. Zoho publishes the wall instead of hiding it, which respects the buyer. The catch is absolute: the moment a fourth person needs access, every tier becomes paid, and there is no per-user metering underneath the free plan. 

### Salesforce Free Suite and Pipedrive's trial

 Salesforce's Free Suite, listed at $0 on its pricing page, is the newest entry, and its published limits sit well below Starter Suite, so treat it as a sampling tool rather than a working tier. Pipedrive skips the question entirely: no free plan, a 14-day full-access trial instead. Between the two approaches, Zoho's flat 3-user offer remains the only free tier a small team can build on for years. 

## Which CRM Wins on Price?

 Entry stickers cluster between $14 and $25, so the honest comparison starts at the team level. These figures use annual billing and each vendor's published October 2026 prices. 

| CRM | Entry tier (annual/seat) | Automation tier (annual/seat) | 5 seats, entry tier | Month-to-month? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zoho CRM | $14 (Standard) | $23 (Professional) | $70/mo | Yes, all tiers |
| Pipedrive | $14 (Lite) | $39 (Growth) | $70/mo | Yes, ~42% more |
| HubSpot | $20 Starter ($7 annual) | $90 (Sales Professional) | $100/mo list | Below Professional only |
| Salesforce | $25 (Starter Suite) | $100 (Pro Suite) | $125/mo | Starter only |

 At entry level, Zoho and Pipedrive tie at $70 monthly for five people, and the tiebreaks are philosophical: Zoho throws in workflows at $23 per user, whereas Pipedrive charges $39 for automation but delivers the cleaner interface. The spread explodes at ten seats with automation needs. Zoho Professional costs $230 monthly, Pipedrive Growth $390, HubSpot Sales Professional $900 plus the mandatory $1,500 onboarding fee, and Salesforce Pro Suite $1,000 on an annual contract. That is a 4x spread between the cheapest and priciest path to the same outcome. 

 One more figure worth writing down: HubSpot splits Starter by billing term, $20 per seat monthly versus $7 on annual commitments, with the annual rate reserved for new customers. Planning around the new-customer rate is how budgets get surprised in year two. 

## Our Take

 If we were spending our own money today, Zoho CRM is the default answer for teams under 20 people. The $14 Standard tier does what most buyers actually need from a CRM, month-to-month billing keeps the exit door open, and the free 3-user plan means the smallest teams pay nothing at all. Its interface is the least charming of the four, and we would take that trade every time at these prices. 

 HubSpot earns the top overall spot for a different reason: no rival makes the free-to-paid journey this smooth, and none connects marketing to sales in one database this cleanly. But we would enter at Starter and pause hard before Sales Professional, because $90 per seat plus $1,500 onboarding plus contact pricing is a commitment that deserves a spreadsheet of its own. Pipedrive is the tool we would hand a founder-led sales team that hates software training, with the warning that automation starts at Growth's $39, not Lite's $14. Salesforce we would buy only with an admin already in the plan, because unconfigured Salesforce is the most expensive spreadsheet on the market. 

## Sources & References

- HubSpot Sales Hub pricing (official)
- HubSpot product and services catalog: seat types, credits, onboarding fees
- Salesforce Sales Cloud pricing (official)
- Pipedrive pricing: Lite, Growth, Premium, Ultimate (official)
- Zoho CRM pricing and editions (official)

## Final Verdict

 Every recommendation above rests on vendor pricing pages and published plan documentation verified in October 2026, not on tests we ran ourselves. Our take, after running the team-level math: 

 HubSpot is the best CRM for most buyers in 2026 because the free tier is real and the platform grows with you, provided you treat Sales Professional as a considered purchase rather than an upgrade. Zoho CRM is the value winner at $14 per user with month-to-month freedom and the only free plan a small team can live on for years. Pipedrive takes the simplicity crown with its rebuilt $14-to-$79 lineup, and its 2026 rebrand is a reason to distrust older comparison articles, including any still listing Essential and Advanced plans. Salesforce remains the endgame for scale, with a fair $25 entry point and the highest ceiling in the category, bought best alongside an admin budget. 

## Frequently Asked Questions

 What is the best CRM software overall in 2026? 

For most small and mid-size teams, HubSpot is the strongest starting point: the core CRM is free, Starter lists at $20 per seat per month, and marketing, sales and service data live in one place from day one. Zoho CRM beats it on raw value once you pay, at $14 per user monthly on the Standard tier with month-to-month billing and a free 3-user plan underneath. Pipedrive wins for teams that want nothing but a clean sales pipeline, and Salesforce only makes sense when customization at scale is a hard requirement, since its costs and admin needs grow fastest.

 Is there a free CRM in 2026 that stays free? 

Two of the four qualify. Zoho CRM is the honest one: up to 3 users free forever, with 5,000 API calls per day and data export allowed up to 10 times. HubSpot's free tier is broader but capped at basic usage, 10 custom properties and 1,000 contacts, with HubSpot branding on every email and form. Salesforce now lists a Free Suite at $0, though its published limits sit well below Starter Suite, which is the real self-service entry at $25 per user. Pipedrive offers no free plan at all, only a 14-day trial.

 How much should a small team budget for a CRM? 

On annual billing, a 5-person team pays about $70 per month for Zoho CRM Standard or Pipedrive Lite, $100 for HubSpot Starter at list price, or $125 for Salesforce Starter Suite. Those entry figures mislead less than they seem to: the real dividing line appears at the automation tier. A 10-person team needing automation pays $230 monthly on Zoho Professional, $390 on Pipedrive Growth, $900 on HubSpot Sales Professional plus a mandatory $1,500 onboarding fee, or $1,000 on Salesforce Pro Suite with an annual contract.

 Did Pipedrive change its plans in 2026? 

Yes. The old five-tier ladder of Essential, Advanced, Professional, Power and Enterprise has been replaced by four plans: Lite at $14, Growth at $39, Premium at $59 and Ultimate at $79 per seat monthly on annual billing. The functional boundaries moved too. Automation, email sequences and full email sync now start at Growth, and what used to be separate selling points, such as lead routing and e-signatures, bundle into Premium. Many comparison articles still publish the retired ladder, so double-check any Pipedrive figure you read against the vendor's own pricing page.

 Which CRM gets expensive the fastest? 

HubSpot, once you cross into Professional. Sales Hub Professional costs $90 per seat monthly on an annual commitment, and HubSpot adds a mandatory, non-refundable onboarding fee of $1,500 at that tier ($3,500 at Enterprise, $3,000 on Marketing Hub Professional). Seat types complicate it further: Core seats and Sales seats are priced separately, and mixing subscription levels reprices every seat in the account to the highest tier. Salesforce climbs highest overall at $195 to $550 per user on full Sales Cloud editions, but its cost curve is more predictable.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Questions?

- What are AI credits?

AI credits power the specific tools your team needs most, from AI Agents to Meeting Notetakers. Instead of a one-size-fits-all fee, credits reflect the complexity of each task, meaning you only pay for the work actually done. A typical 3-person team thrives on ~800–1,200 credits per month. To put that into perspective, 1,000 credits can cover roughly 50 resume screenings, 5 hours of meeting summaries, and hundreds of automated workflow updates. You can track your usage in real-time and purchase more whenever your team needs to scale. Learn more about credits
- Is there a free version of monday.com?

monday.com has a free plan of monday work management which is ideal for freelancers and individual professionals. In addition, we offer a 14-day free trial of the Pro plan for monday work management, monday CRM and monday dev.
- How much does monday.com cost?

monday.com cost depends on the plan you choose and your team size. Plans start from 3 users. If you want to sign up more than 40 users, you can request a quote to get an exact price.
- Can you pay for monday.com monthly?

Yes, you can pay monthly for your account. Choose the monthly option on the pricing page and you will be able to pay on a per-month basis. The monthly plan is not discounted so if you are looking to save, we recommend the yearly plan.
- Which pricing plan is right for me?

We understand that each organization is unique, requiring specific features to support its workflows and projects. Above you can see the features included in the different plans to support your needs. If you need help in choosing the right plan for you, check out this article or reach out to our sales team.
- How does our pricing work?

Our pricing is based on two factors; the feature plan you’d like to use, and the number of users on the platform. Once you’ve decided on the feature plan and users, choose your preferred subscription payment: month-to-month or annual. Payment is made in one upfront installment. If you purchase a plan for one year, you will pay for one year upfront.
- What if I change my mind?

If you've paid for a yearly subscription in the last 30 days, and wish to cancel your account, you are entitled to a partial refund. Meaning, we will automatically refund you the remaining balance from your original purchase. Simply cancel the account from the Admin section, and your account will be automatically refunded. If you have any questions, you can always reach out to our support team
- Do you offer any discounted plans?

Yes, by choosing a yearly plan, you will receive an 18% discount.
- Does monday.com offer plans to nonprofits and NGOs?

monday.com is a proud supporter of organizations that do great things around the world. That’s why we offer discounted pricing for qualified nonprofit organisations. Click here to find out more about our nonprofit plan and pricing.
- How can I manage my billing?

If you are an admin of your account, you can access your purchase history, invoices, payment details, plan type, and more. Learn how to manage your billing details here.
- Can I change my plan?

You can make changes to your plan at any time by changing your plan type and by adding or removing users. However, past the refund period, we offer no refunds for downgrades. To change your plan, simply go into the Admin section and click on the Billing option. From there, click 'change plan' and choose your desired plan.
- How secure is monday.com?

The security of our customer’s data is our top priority. We use advanced security measures to preserve the integrity and privacy of your data, and adhere to strict data protection laws. monday.com is built with internationally recognized security standards and protocols in place, such as ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27018, and we undergo annual security audits and assessments. 
- What payment methods do you accept?

We accept payments from the following major credit cards, excluding debit cards; Visa, Master Card, American Express, Discover, Diners Club, JCB, Carte Bleue, Union Pay. You can also purchase your monday.com subscription with PayPal. Please note this may be subject to change depending on your location. In addition, we accept invoices for Enterprise orders that meet a minimum fee - Feel free to reach out to our support team for more information.
- Do you have mobile apps?

Yes, the platform is available on both IOS and Android devices. You can download them on the Apple or Google Play Stores. Learn more here.
